themes.title: Make my direction clear
themes.outcome: Position an aspiring AI consultant around useful problems and a transparent approach.

themes.title: Build trust through evidence
themes.outcome: Let projects, sources, and honest reflection demonstrate my current capabilities.

themes.title: Make collaboration easy
themes.outcome: Give visitors a clear next step and learn from their feedback.

stories.title: Understand my focus
stories.story: As a prospective collaborator, I want to understand my AI and Information Systems focus so I can decide whether to explore my work.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The hero identifies Ximena, Information Systems at NJIT, expected graduation January 2029, and an aspiring AI consulting / FDE direction. It makes no claim of established client experience.

tasks.description: Draft a concise positioning statement.
Connect the hero to Projects and Consulting Approach.
Check education details and remove unsupported claims.

stories.title: Choose my next step
stories.story: As a first-time visitor, I want to find the main areas of the portfolio so I can reach relevant evidence quickly.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Career research, projects, consulting approach, and contact are reachable through clearly labeled links. Links work on narrow screens and by keyboard.

tasks.description: Simplify the main navigation.
Add descriptive calls to action.
Check page destinations and keyboard focus.

stories.title: Explore proposed capabilities
stories.story: As a prospective collaborator, I want to see the types of work I am developing toward so I can assess whether a conversation would be useful.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The page describes workflow discovery, scoped AI prototyping, and evaluation/documentation as developing capabilities. Each has an example deliverable and a clear scope limit.

tasks.description: Draft three capability descriptions.
Connect each to relevant existing work or a labeled future project.
Review wording so learning goals are distinct from delivered services.

stories.title: Understand the process
stories.story: As a project partner, I want to understand the steps from discovery to handoff so I know how the work could be scoped and reviewed.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Discover → Define → Prototype → Evaluate → Handoff is explained. Each step names an output and a feedback checkpoint; no guaranteed business results are promised.

tasks.description: Write an example discovery brief and success criteria.
Show the five process steps with deliverables.
Add a change-request and scope-review checkpoint.

stories.title: Browse relevant projects
stories.story: As a technical reviewer, I want to filter projects by skill and project type so I can find evidence relevant to a role or problem.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Project cards show a short summary, relevant skills, repository link, and an honest status. Filters distinguish software, web/design, research, and introductory exercises; clearing filters restores all projects.

tasks.description: Reuse the reviewed public-repository summaries.
Add category metadata and accessible filter controls.
Check combined filters, reset, and an empty-result state.

stories.title: Inspect source evidence
stories.story: As a technical reviewer, I want to open the source behind a project claim so I can assess the evidence myself.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Repository and evidence links are labeled and match each summary. Team projects identify shared ownership. Private repositories and empty exercises are not presented as completed client work.

tasks.description: Verify the source link for each featured claim.
Keep starter, unfinished, and team labels visible.
Check external links and document the review date.

stories.title: Understand a case study
stories.story: As a portfolio reviewer, I want to understand a project’s problem, approach, and result so I can assess relevant engineering and delivery reasoning.
stories.acceptance_criteria: At least one case study contains context, problem, scope, approach, evidence, and limitations. Results distinguish observed behavior from proposed benefits; no client, metric, or outcome is invented. Technical reviewers can find the implementation flow, source links, and a documented check or an explicit evidence gap. Delivery reviewers can find intended users, scope, and the evidence or unmeasured status of the outcome.

tasks.description: Choose one repository with sufficient evidence.
Write the problem, implementation flow, and source links.
Add verification evidence, outcome labels, and a verified screenshot or demo when available.
Review the case study using both persona perspectives.

stories.title: Understand my contribution
stories.story: As a hiring manager, I want to distinguish my contribution and learning from team or AI assistance so I can assess my actual experience.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The case study labels individual, team, template, and AI-assisted work where applicable. Unconfirmed ownership is marked for confirmation; a learning reflection identifies a concrete decision or limitation.

tasks.description: Ask Ximena to confirm her contribution.
Document tool or template assistance accurately.
Review every ownership and proficiency statement.

stories.title: Understand my background
stories.story: As a recruiter, I want to see my education and relevant experience so I can place my projects in context.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Education uses the updated major and January 2029 date. Customer-facing, leadership, and programming experience is tied to the résumé without assuming old roles are current.

tasks.description: Adapt the existing profile into a concise About section.
Connect transferable experience to project examples.
Confirm current role dates before changing their status.

stories.title: Review my career reasoning
stories.story: As a professor or mentor, I want to follow the sources and reasoning behind my career choices so I can give specific feedback.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The existing three-career comparison remains linked, including source dates, eligibility limitations, and the roadmap. Proposed consulting positioning does not imply those job requirements are already met.

tasks.description: Link the current career research and roadmap.
Cross-check source and timeline labels.
Ask a reviewer to locate an original employer source.

stories.title: Start a conversation
stories.story: As a prospective collaborator, I want to find a clear way to contact me so I can discuss a project, internship, or feedback.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A contact section links to the existing LinkedIn profile and names useful conversation topics. It does not imply that a form submission or booking system exists.

tasks.description: Add the verified LinkedIn link.
Draft a short invitation and suggested message topics.
Check the link and accessible label.

stories.title: Prepare a useful inquiry
stories.story: As a potential project partner, I want to see what information to include in my message so our first conversation has a clear starting point.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A short checklist asks for the problem, intended users, available non-sensitive sample data, constraints, and desired outcome. It avoids requesting passwords, credentials, or private customer records.

tasks.description: Write a five-item discovery checklist.
Explain that scope is agreed after discussion.
Review with one classmate for clarity.
